answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not yet on either. Next week stays at about 18 easy miles, and speedwork waits until the week of Nov 9 – 15 at the earliest.

Feeling ready is a good sign, and your three runs back this week support it. You had no pain, and by Sunday your easy pace and heart rate were back to normal. But 12 to 40 miles is more than triple the load, a week after a marathon you ran at effort 9/10. Muscles feel ready before tendons and other connective tissue are.

Here is a sensible way back if the legs stay pain-free. Run about 18 miles this week, the mid 20s the week after, and the low 30s after that. Aim for 40 no sooner than the week of Nov 16 – 22. Light strides this week, then a short session in the week of Nov 9 – 15, would be the first speed.

If you want to race the Thanksgiving 10K, tell me and I will shape those weeks around it. Your marathon fitness is still there, and a short sharpening block is enough for a 10K.

new.analysis:
Last week went exactly as planned. You ran all three easy runs at the planned distance, 12 miles in total, and every minute with heart rate recorded sat in zones 1 and 2. Pain was 0/10 each time, which is the result I wanted from a first week back.

The runs also show the legs returning in order. Your first run averaged 10:49 per mile at heart rate 128. By Sunday you were at 9:51 and heart rate 139, your normal easy effort from before the race, and it felt like 3/10. That tells me the muscles you can feel have recovered. It says less about tendons and connective tissue, which recover more slowly.

That gap is why I'm capping this week at about 18 miles. You ran 26.2 miles at effort 9/10 on Sun Oct 18, and a quick jump in load before the body has fully rebuilt is a common way runners get hurt after a race. Your fitness was built over weeks of 34 to 46 miles, and a few easy weeks won't take it away.

Nothing this week asks for speed. Most runs have a rest day on one side, and a few relaxed strides on Saturday are a light reminder of faster running. They are only a reminder, so skip them if the legs feel heavy.

You missed 3:45 by about five minutes after holding goal pace through 20 miles. That deserves a proper look at fueling and the final miles once I know what comes next, but not this week.
